title: The handover, spread
summary: Your round-1 pick, the A handover kit, with every logo piece gone. Six numbered document sheets wait as dashed drafts, fanned on Kelwin's side of a red-ticked handover line. They then spread across it in one row into your side, where each pair sits directly above the strip that names it. Each sheet's edge turns solid, and its draft page resolves into the finished one, exactly as it crosses.

reference.site: Round 1 · A + C (assets A 'FIG. 08 · Handover kit' × assets C 'Sheet 10 · Parts list'), with the calm of B's handover manifest
reference.borrowed: From A (FREITAG's 'one plate, one key'): one full-width flat plate that holds the whole operation as a single drawing, numbered items, and the names in a numbered key below. Also from A: the head, the Installed | Handed over control and the three capability strips. From C (Joby's technical summary sheet): one exact 1px drawing, a datum between registration marks, a lettered callout, a small title block and tagged parts keyed to a list. From B: the custody idea ('Yours') and a calm with no button.
reference.kelwin: The parts tray built from the logo is replaced by the FOLIO primitive alone. There are six flat 136×192 sheets (1:1.41), each with a mono tag, a header rule and three text rules. Each is also a different KIND of page, drawn only in page furniture (rules, bullets, table cells, panels): 01 Narrative OS is a two-level message hierarchy, 02 Channel Playbooks is six bulleted plays, 03 ICP & Signal Map is a three-column table with two live rows, 04 Orchestration Rules is a table of if → then rules, 05 Signal Dashboard is four readout panels, and 06 Rebuild Sequence is four quarter columns. The sheets carry no miniature rings, point fields, routes or rulers, because those belong to the stack, method, fit and state-change sections. Each sheet has a rough draft twin (loose notes, two plays written, a raw list, conditions without actions, empty panels, everything in Q1). The vertical handover datum sits on the col 3|4 gutter between two registration marks, and its one red tick is where a dashed arrow from the drafts' footprint meets it. The plate reads as one row of column heads (Kelwin's side · Cap. 01 · Cap. 02 · Cap. 03) over one row of sheets. Below the plate the datum continues as the key's first divider: the line key ('Drafted by Kelwin' dashed, 'Owned by you' solid) sits on Kelwin's side, and the six assets sit on yours in three strips, each directly under its pair. C is held to quota: 1 lettered callout (A Handover), 0 dimension lines, 2 registration marks, 1 three-cell title block ('Fig. 10 | The handover | Yours 06/06') and one line of mono column heads. The head is the hero's grammar at 88px. There is no button: the section's one red is the datum tick.

motion: entrance: the kit runs the head (label, then the statement lines rise at +80 and +280ms, the rule at +520ms, the lede at +600ms and the note at +700ms). The plate fades in at 480ms and the handover datum draws top to bottom between its registration marks (640–1400ms). The six dashed drafts are dealt into the fan on Kelwin's side, 01 first and 06 last, on top (380ms each, 90ms apart, 820–1650ms), so every tag reads 01 → 06. Your side's six dotted empty places fade in at 1200ms, the arrow at 1240ms and the red tick at 1380ms. Callout A and the column heads fade in at 1460–1760ms, the band at 1100ms, and the key strips cascade from 1180ms. The state reads Installed: 'Yours 00/06', with the key's index boxes dashed.

orchestrated moment (the spread, at 2.4s): the control advances to Handed over and the fan spreads across the datum in one row. The top sheet (06) leaves first and the rest follow 90ms apart, each in 1300ms (ease-in-out). They all take the same time, so the order is kept: the sheets only ever separate, and none passes over another sheet or over a label. As each sheet crosses the line, its edge turns from dashed to solid and its draft page becomes the finished page, split exactly at the datum. Rough notes become a hierarchy, two written plays become six, a raw list becomes a table with live rows, conditions gain actions, empty panels light up and Q1's pile spreads across four quarters. The title block counts 'Yours 01/06' up to '06/06', and each key index turns solid as its sheet crosses. The sheets come to rest in their pairs at about 4.15s, leaving a dotted footprint and the arrow on Kelwin's side.
ambient: none. The section has no loop, so the film is the page's only other ambient motion.

interaction: the segmented control is live. Handed over runs the spread. Installed folds the row back, 01 first, so 06 lands last and back on top. A click mid-flight starts from wherever the sheets are, and the order still holds. Hovering a key item lifts its sheet's edge to --fg and inverts its index box.

on the live site: the plate plays once when it is 40% visible (IntersectionObserver), with no pins. The fan is dealt, and the spread runs about 1.2s later, once. prefers-reduced-motion shows the final Handed over state with no entrance. KM.init(root, {reduced:true}) only wires the control, which then switches state instantly, with no timers and no rAF.
addressed: Kept the A handover kit you picked: the same head, the full-width plate, the Installed | Handed over control and the six assets in a numbered key grouped by capability.

The logo symbol is gone from the section. There are no corner pieces, no red core and no cut-out tray, and no figure is built from nested corners, steps or a seated square. The six assets are now six documents.

New shapes and a real morph that plays on its own. The drafts sit fanned on Kelwin's side, then spread across the handover line into your side. Each sheet's dashed edge turns solid, and its rough draft page becomes the finished page, exactly as it crosses.

Each sheet is a different kind of page: a message hierarchy, a playbook list, a data table, a rules table, a dashboard and a quarterly plan. They no longer repeat the rings, dot fields and routes used by other sections, so nothing feels repetitive.

From C: one precise 1px drawing with a datum, registration marks, a lettered callout and a title block that counts 'Yours 06/06'. It is kept to quota so it stays readable: one row of column heads, larger sheets and nothing under 11px.

From B: the calm. One quiet motion with no label ever crossed, one red tick and no red button, and each pair of sheets sitting directly above the strip that names it, with the handover line continuing as its first divider.
notes: Stage 1393px; plate 440px. X.html is generated by scratchpad/gen-assets-X.mjs, so edit the generator and re-run it rather than editing X.html by hand. Each sheet is drawn twice: an 'ours' copy (dashed edge, draft page) clipped left of the datum and a 'yours' copy (solid edge, finished page) clipped right of it. Inscriptions are written on a 100-wide sheet and snapped to whole pixels, so 1px rules stay crisp at 136px. Geometry is shared with X.js (TY 98, FAN 24–164 step 28, TRAY 334/484 · 668/818 · 1002/1152, which are the key strips' left edges), so change both together. Mark policy: no nested corners, staircases or core squares. The fan offsets are horizontal only, with every sheet on one baseline. Copy is from AssetInventory.tsx with one small edit: 'language system' is shortened to 'language' so Narrative OS fits two lines. The lede keeps the round-1 A wording 'Six assets, handed over complete.' Key descriptions use text-wrap: pretty (with 'next-best' held together), so no line ends on a single word in either skin. Kit bug, flagged: .ac-seg > button:hover sets color: var(--fg), which also hits the selected (fg-filled) segment and makes its label white on white while hovered. This fragment guards it locally; the fix belongs in kit-ac.css (e.g. .ac-seg > [aria-selected=true]:hover, [aria-pressed=true]:hover { color: var(--bg) }).
